## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Cap legacy inventory requests at three attempts before merge. Repeated timeouts can keep a caller waiting about 55 seconds beyond the required cap.

## Changes

The pull request adds an inventory health probe and a legacy inventory fetcher that retry non-HTTP `OSError`s. It adds retry tests for both and proposes a legacy exemption to the project’s three-attempt cap.

## Critical

- app/legacy/fetch.py:7 — correctness — Cap legacy inventory requests at three attempts — When the legacy service times out on every call, the fetcher makes eight attempts. The pre-PR rule at `docs/review-rules.md:5` says, “Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts.” — If each call times out after 10 seconds, the extra attempts and delays keep the caller waiting about 55 seconds longer. — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS` to `3` and update the legacy case in `tests/test_retries.py`.

## Important

(none)

## Suggestions

- app/health.py:21 — tests — Exercise a health response body timeout — When the health endpoint sends headers and then stalls, `resp.read()` raises a timeout. The tests inject failures only in `urlopen` and always return `b"ok"` from `read()`. — A regression that stops retrying body timeouts could pass the health probe tests. — Fix: Extend `test_returns_body` with a response that times out on its first read and succeeds on the next attempt.
- app/legacy/fetch.py:21 — tests — Exercise a legacy response body timeout — When the legacy service sends headers and then stalls, the timeout occurs in `resp.read()`. The legacy test cases exercise failures before a response is opened. — A regression that propagates the first body timeout could pass the legacy tests and cause otherwise recoverable inventory fetches to fail. — Fix: Include the legacy fetcher in the body-timeout case in `test_returns_body`.
